sentences.text: The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner.

9. PW 1 in his evidence filed by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A, has deposed that on 11.06.2017, at about 1.00 P.M, he was going from his village to Najafgarh via Hiran Kundra on his scooter bearing No. HR13A0155.
When he was around Nilwal Mor, a swift car bearing No. DL 2CAP6527 being driven by R.1 came from Dichaon side at a very high speed, rashly and negligently in the middle of the road.
The driver of car applied brakes recklessly due to which the car turned around and back side of the car hit his scooter.
As a result of which he fell down on road and received grievous injuries on his both legs .

He has deposed that he was firstly taken to Swastik Hospital,Nazafgarh,Delhi and thereafter shifted to Dr Mukesh Orthopedic & Trauma Centre,
Bawana Road,Narela Delhi.
He remained admitted in hospital from 11.06.2017 to 14.06.2017.
10.PW 1 has been crossexamined, but nothing material could come out MACT No. 1040/17 Jai Bhagwan Vs Jatin Yadav & Ors Page No. 8 of 15 from his cross examination which could disbelief his testimony.

sentences.text: Being injured, the petitioner was the natural eyewitness of the accident.
Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing off a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim was at fault, in any way.
11.The fact that petitioner suffered injuries in that accident is also supported by his medical documents.
After investigation, police also indicted respondent no. 1 as accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338 IPC.
The case has been registered against respondent no. 1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his alleged false implication, if any.
The fact of accident and the respondent no.1 is facing the trial as an accused is not disputed.

Considering all these facts, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of car bearing No. DL 2CAP6527 by respondent no. 1 thereby causing injuries to the petitioner.
ISSUE No.2: ? Whether the petitioner in the above mentioned case is entitled to claim compensation , if so , what amount and from whom? ... OPO 12.
Being injured, petitioner is well within his rights to claim compensation.

It is there on record, as per the deposition of PW 1 and the MLC annexed with DAR, that he was firstly taken to Swastik Hospital,Nazafgarh,Delhi and thereafter shifted to Dr Mukesh Orthopedic & Trauma Centre,
Bawana Road,Narela Delhi.

It is deposed by him (PW1) that due to the said accident, he himself and his MACT No. 1040/17 Jai Bhagwan Vs Jatin Yadav & Ors Page No. 9 of 15 family members have suffered great mental pain, agony, love and affection, loss of income, loss of social activities etc.

His ability to earn in future has to be kept in mind while awarding compensation to injured.
In the case in hand, the date of accident is 11.06.2017
At that time the petitioner was working as Stamp Vendor.

This Tribunal has already assessed in preceding para, the income of injured under Minimum Wages Act prevailing in Haryana, under the head of Skilled labour as Rs.10,064.62/ P.M. in the year 2017.
As per disability certificate of the petitioner he has suffered 10% ( Ten percent) permanent disability in relation right lower limb.
The petitioner was about 50 years of age at the time of accident.

In view of paragraph no. 61 (iv) of judgment in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors, SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, decided on 31.10.2017 and the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case of Sanjay Oberoi vs Manoj Bageriya, MAC Appeal no.829/2011 decided on 03.11.2017, the injured would be entitled to an addition of 25% of the established income.

The next point that is to be discussed is pain and suffering and to calculate the same, the nature of injuries caused to the injured due to the accident, duration for which he got medical treatment and he was constrained to live in bed are few factors which must be taken into account.
After the accident, petitioner was firstly taken to Swastik Hospital,Nazafgarh,Delhi and thereafter shifted to Dr Mukesh Orthopedic & Trauma Centre, Bawana Road,Narela Delhi.
He remained admitted in hospital from 11.06.2017 to 14.06.2017.
There are injuries on his both the legs.
It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the mental agony which he faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
To compensate petitioner under this head, a sum of Rs.50,000/ is awarded to him.

6. After competition of pleading, vide an order dated 12.01.2018, the following issues were framed in the present case:
(i) Whether Jai Bhagwan S/O Sh Ram Chander sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt.
11.06.2017 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle ( Car) No. DL2CAP6527 being driven by R1 Jatin Yadav, Owned by Respondent NO. 2 Jai Bhagwan and Insured by R3 National Insurance Company ?
OPP (ii) Whether the petitioner in the above mentioned case is entitled to claim compensation if so, what amount and from whom?
ISSUE No.2: ? Whether the petitioner in the above mentioned case is entitled to claim compensation , if so , what amount and from whom? ... OPO 12.
opennyai_summary.facts:
As a result of which he fell down on road and received grievous injuries on his both legs.
Being injured, the petitioner was the natural eyewitness of the accident.
Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing off a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
After investigation, police also indicted respondent no. 1 as accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338 IPC.
The case has been registered against respondent no. 1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his alleged false implication, if any.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim was at fault, in any way.
11.The fact that petitioner suffered injuries in that accident is also supported by his medical documents.
Considering all these facts, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of car bearing No. DL 2CAP6527 by respondent no. 1 thereby causing injuries to the petitioner.
Being injured, petitioner is well within his rights to claim compensation.
His ability to earn in future has to be kept in mind while awarding compensation to injured.
In the case in hand, the date of accident is 11.06.2017
At that time the petitioner was working as Stamp Vendor.
However he has not filed any documents with regarding to his earning.
As per disability certificate of the petitioner he has suffered 10% ( Ten percent) permanent disability in relation right lower limb.
The petitioner was about 50 years of age at the time of accident.
In view of paragraph no. 61 (iv) of judgment in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors, SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, decided on 31.10.2017 and the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case of Sanjay Oberoi vs Manoj Bageriya, MAC Appeal no.829/2011 decided on 03.11.2017, the injured would be entitled to an addition of 25% of the established income.
It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the mental agony which he faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
